name: Stanley Black & Decker, Inc.
moat_justification: DEWALT's professional brand and battery-platform lock-in are real, but share is contested by Milwaukee, the consumer brands are weak, and returns collapsed through the last downturn — no through-cycle pricing power proof.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.5%) vs bull-case tier C (12.6%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Turnaround in progress with a real DEWALT franchise, moat 5/10 — but even on the generous TTM base it returns 9.9% weighted (IV@15% $55.43 vs $92.48); it only clears 15% at ~$55 or below.
moat_for: DEWALT professional brand equity and trust (~17% dollar share in power tools)
20V MAX / FLEXVOLT battery ecosystem lock-in for professional users
Distribution scale across Home Depot, Lowe's and pro channels
Engineered fastening niches with co-engineered, qualified auto/aerospace positions
moat_against: TTI's Milwaukee gaining professional share with faster cordless innovation
Retailer private labels and low-cost Chinese brands eroding the consumer tier
Housing/DIY cyclicality — gross margin fell 37% to 25% in the 2022-23 downturn
Peak ROIC only mid-teens (8.8-15.0% where computable), not through-cycle high
